body:
### Summary

When run as root, `uv pip compile requirements.in -o /dev/null` deletes the `/dev/null`
character device and puts a regular file holding the compiled requirements in its place.

The cause is how the output file is written. `OutputWriter::commit()`
(`crates/uv-command-support/src/lib.rs:123`) calls `uv_fs::write_atomic()`
(`crates/uv-fs/src/lib.rs:487`). That function creates a temp file in the target's parent
directory and renames it over the target. Nothing checks first whether the target is a
device, FIFO or socket. The only special case today is following symlinks.

`-o /dev/null` is a natural thing to type when you only want to know whether a resolution
succeeds. We hit this when an automated agent did exactly that inside a Docker container,
where `/dev` is a root-writable tmpfs:

- Nothing failed visibly at first.
- From then on, every program that daemonizes with glibc's `daemon()` broke, because it
  rejects a `/dev/null` that isn't char device 1,3. For example, every new tmux server died
  with `server exited unexpectedly`.
- Anything reading `/dev/null` got stale content instead of EOF.
- It took `mknod` or a container restart to recover.

**Minimal reproduction** (uses a scratch device node instead of the real `/dev/null`):

```console
# mkdir t && cd t
# printf 'six==1.16.0\n' > req.in
# mknod -m 666 null c 1 3
# stat -c '%F %t,%T %s' null
character special file 1,3 0
# uv pip compile req.in --no-deps -o null
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv pip compile req.in --no-deps -o null
six==1.16.0
    # via -r req.in
# stat -c '%F %s' null
regular file 144
```

The same command with `-o /dev/null`, run as root, does this to the real `/dev/null`.

**Expected:** writing to an existing non-regular file, such as `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout` or
a FIFO, opens the file and writes to it, without the temp-file-and-rename. Alternatively,
uv refuses the path with an error. It should never replace the file. For `/dev/null` (and
`NUL` on Windows) uv could simply skip writing.

Other `write_atomic` callers that take a user-supplied path probably need the same check.

### Platform

Debian 13 (trixie) x86_64, Linux 6.1.0-53-amd64, running as root in a Docker container

### Version

uv 0.13.0 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu), installed with pip

### Python version

Python 3.12.15
title: `uv pip compile -o /dev/null` replaces the /dev/null device with a regular file (atomic write over non-regular files)
